value.name: takes briefcase to the door
value.description: Asha lifts the briefcase from the desk and carries it toward the door, pausing before leaving the study.
evidence: Asha lifted the briefcase off the desk and carried it to the door, where she stopped with her hand on the jamb and looked back once at the lamp burning over the empty pad.

value.name: checks the lock twice
value.description: She tests the door lock twice, making sure the bolt is properly seated before she leaves.
evidence: She tested the lock, then tested it again, the bolt clicking softly the second time though she had heard it seat the first.

value.name: turns off the study lamp
value.description: Asha switches off the lamp, leaving the study dark and forcing her to confront the permanence of her decision.
evidence: When she was satisfied she reached for the switch and put the lamp out, and the study went dark all at once, the desk and the closed briefcase and the chair she had been sitting in for hours dropping out of sight together.

She stood another moment in that dark with her hand still on the switch, because the room without the light was only a room, and what she had decided in it would have to hold under different lamps in the morning.

value.name: leaves the study in darkness
value.description: In the dark hallway, Asha carries the briefcase out without turning on the hall light and gathers her coat and keys by touch.
evidence: In the dark hallway Asha shifted the briefcase from her left hand to her right and felt the latched weight settle against her hip, the leather still cool from the study.
She did not turn on the hall light.
She found her coat by touch, slid the keys from the dish by the door, and stepped out onto the stoop, pulling the door shut behind her until the bolt caught.

value.name: places briefcase on passenger seat
value.description: Asha sets the briefcase flat on the passenger seat so the trial notes lie level and keeps the marked page between herself and the windshield.
evidence: The briefcase went onto the passenger seat rather than the floor, set flat so the spine of the trial notes lay level, and she sat a moment with her hand on the lid before she put the key in the ignition, registering that the page with the circled marks was now between her and the windshield
